body:
4,248 leads at ₹16.58 each.

That was the cheapest cost per lead I had ever produced, for a Tirupur apparel manufacturer, across six campaigns.

Cheap leads and leads that close are two different products.

The form asked nothing. Two taps, every field pre-filled from Facebook. So Meta went and found the cheapest person who would do a thing that costs nothing to do — because that is exactly what the ad and form asked for.

That business, Nova Attire, did convert some of those leads into sample orders and a bulk order or two each. But nothing in the setup captured the second order. No reorder timing, no follow-up when a buyer's stock would run low. A lead who said "not interested" was marked closed for good, even though some came back on their own, months later, and ordered.

If your cost per lead dropped last month, open Ads Manager and check what the form actually asked for. A form with no real question gets you the cheapest person willing to tap twice, not the buyer who reorders.

What does your cheapest-performing ad set actually ask someone to do before they count as a lead?
